A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with complete main text and Appendices A.1–A.14. Text extraction and visual inspection support reliable comparison of their equations, figures, tables and algorithms.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments measuring classification loss, sparsity, runtime, Rashomon-set approximation and variable importance in Section 7 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including the additional benchmark comparisons and predictive-multiplicity analysis in the appendices.

M1.justification: The specified bound routine receives limited corrections: Algorithms 1 and 12 change the depth check from d = d_l to d' = d_l, and Algorithm 1 changes error normalization from |D| to global N. Normalization by N already appeared in v2 Algorithm 12. The algorithm family and postprocessing remain unchanged; these corrections do not establish experimental reruns.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ten datasets and retain the same classification, Rashomon-set and variable-importance evaluations. The citations added in Appendix A.7.1 document existing datasets rather than introduce new coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator participation is unchanged, including CART/greedy, GOSDT, Top-k (DL8.5), TSDT, MAPTree, Murtree, Blossom and the Tsallis-entropy method. GOSDT and Murtree remain excluded from the depth-6 comparisons in both versions.

E3.justification: Section 7 and Appendix A.7 retain the same splits, depth and lookahead settings, preprocessing, hyperparameter searches and time limits. The subproblem-normalization corrections do not report a revised experimental protocol or evaluation metric.

E4.justification: The lookahead-depth sensitivity, binarization comparisons, postprocessing analysis, feature-scaling experiments, RID analyses and predictive-multiplicity study are retained. No ablation, robustness test or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both report three random train/test splits with standard errors, five-trial Blossom comparisons with 95% confidence intervals, and ten bootstrapped datasets for RID. Run counts and uncertainty-reporting practices throughout the appendices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Reported numerical results and plotted findings match, including Tables 1–18. For example, Table 1 retains Bike runtimes of 14330 seconds for the full computation and 194 seconds for RESPLIT, with correlation 0.999. No result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: Equation 1 changes its summation limit from N to |D| while distinguishing subsets from the global dataset. Equation 4 changes error denominators to N and removes the d' = 0 case. Section 5.1 corrects the rescaling factor from |D(u)|/|D| to |D|/|D(u)|. The runtime and optimality theorems and appendix proofs are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about near-optimal sparse trees, large runtime savings, and scalable Rashomon-set approximation. The stated contributions and their scope are unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning greedy splits near leaves, sparsity/runtime tradeoffs, threshold guessing's optimality cost and RESPLIT's variable-importance fidelity remain unchanged. No substantive limitation, failure condition or applicability boundary is added.

D1.justification: Appendix A.12 explicitly initializes N = |D| and passes N through child-node creation and bound routines. Added dataset-source citations and repository identifiers improve provenance. The code link, hardware specifications, preprocessing instructions and experimental hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Eight dataset-source references are added, including Larson et al. (2016) for COMPAS, Manickam et al. (2022) for HIV and several UCI dataset records. Section 2's methodological related work and research positioning are unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized prose revisions clarify global versus subproblem dataset size and regularization rescaling in Sections 3 and 5.1. Acknowledgements are expanded. The narrative, section order and appendix organization are retained.

P2.justification: The shortened Equation 4 block shifts Algorithm 1 upward and moves the beginning of the postprocessing discussion from page 6 to page 5. References and dataset descriptions reflow. Figures 1–23 and Tables 1–18 retain their displays and content.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects v2's inverted rescaling explanation and depth checks, makes global normalization more explicit, and supplies missing dataset sources. These provide limited clarity and reproducibility gains with unchanged empirical support. The technical repair is incomplete: Equation 1's new subset sum also scales the leaf penalty, inconsistently with Equation 4, and Algorithm 10's root call omits the newly required N argument.
